desc: NM0821-I is a compact, low-power LoRa concentrator board based on the SX1303 with 2 × SX1250 radios, an onboard GPS and an I2C temperature sensor. Compared with the SX1301, it offers higher sensitivity, lower power consumption and a lower operating temperature. It communicates with its host over SPI and lets you develop your own LoRaWAN gateway hassle-free.

overview: NM0821-I is an SX1303 based, compact and low-power LoRa concentrator board with 2 × SX1250 radios, an onboard GPS and an I2C based on-board temperature sensor. Compared with the SX1301 LoRa chip, it offers higher sensitivity, lower power consumption and a lower operating temperature.

It supports SPI based communication with the host. An advanced fine time-stamp feature helps to identify the estimated geo-location. The board is designed for M2M and IoT applications and can be widely applied in LoRaWAN gateways.

The concentrator needs a host system (a PC or an MCU/single-board computer) connected over SPI, and it can receive several LoRa packets simultaneously on different spreading factors and channels. A Raspberry Pi 20 × 2 pin compatible header, UFL and SMA antenna connectors and status LEDs make it a quick starting point for your own LoRaWAN gateway.
